text:
Vegas won this one on the scoreboard by more than it did on the ice. VGK finished with 3.95 expected goals to SEA's 2.58 and would win a simulated replay of every shot 72 percent of the time, a clear edge but nowhere near a 6-2 game. The gap was mostly Joey Daccord, who faced 21 shots and allowed five, about 2.5 goals more than the chances against him deserved.

The damage came in the first two periods. Victor Olofsson deflected one in at 13:02 of the first, Tomas Hertl scored on the power play 2:56 later, and Mark Stone made it 3-0 shorthanded early in the second. The period itself was Vegas's, 1.52 expected goals to 0.43, and Olofsson and Jack Eichel added goals before the intermission, the second coming at 19:29. Seattle's best look, a 36 percent chance for Shane Wright in the first, was stopped by Carter Hart. Philipp Grubauer, pulled after seven shots and one goal against, graded out slightly better than expected, so the early hole was not on him.

Seattle made the third period respectable. Wright beat Hart at 4:52, Hertl answered on the power play at 9:43, and Jared McCann scored on the man advantage at 15:00 after taking seven shots on goal. Hertl finished with two goals and two assists, Eichel with a goal and three assists, and Olofsson with two goals, and the three took the stars. Seattle took 43 penalty minutes to Vegas's 22, though the power-play chances ended up even at five apiece.
